D002_m001.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—actually, if I’m honest, it’s been pretty much my whole life, but it’s gotten harder to ignore lately. As an ER nurse, my job is fast-paced and demanding, and I used to think I handled it well. But lately, I’m making little mistakes—like misreading medication dosages or skipping steps in charting—and that scares me. I’ll start a task, like organizing patient reports, and then forget to finish it because something else grabs my attention. It’s not that I don’t care; I just… lose the thread.

I’ve always had trouble focusing, even back in nursing school. I’d read the same paragraph three times and still not absorb it. People say, “You’re smart, you’ll figure it out,” but it feels like I’m constantly playing catch-up. At home, I can’t seem to finish simple things—laundry piles up, bills go unpaid until the last minute. My mind jumps around, and I’ll be thinking about five unrelated things at once.  

I don’t fidget or pace, but inside, I feel this constant restlessness, like my brain is always running in overdrive. I’ve never been able to sit still with my thoughts. It’s exhausting.
D002_m001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D002_m002.question:

I run my own tailoring business from home, and I used to take such pride in the details—matching patterns, clean seams, finishing touches. Lately, though, I’ve caught myself making little mistakes—wrong measurements, uneven hems—and I don’t even notice until the client points it out. It’s embarrassing. I’ll start a repair or a new piece, lay out the fabric, and then get pulled into something else: the phone rings, the neighbor stops by, or I just start thinking about something completely off track, like what I need at the grocery store or a memory from years ago. Next thing I know, the project’s sitting unfinished, and I’ve lost my momentum.

I try to make lists, set reminders, but I still don’t always follow through, even when I want to. My daughter reminds me to bill clients or return clothes, and I forget. I feel restless inside, like I can’t settle down, even when I’m sitting at the machine. It’s not that I’m moving around constantly, but there’s this internal buzz, like my mind’s always half somewhere else. Honestly, it’s been like this as far back as I can remember—even as a child, my teachers would say I was “daydreamy” or “not quite all there.” I just thought I was bad at focusing. But now it’s starting to affect my work, and I’m worried.
D002_m002.options:
